source.archive: Cui, Li, and Zhou OSF replication archive
source.source_article: Newman, Fast, and Harmon (2020), When eliminating bias isn’t fair: Algorithmic reductionism and procedural justice in human resource decisions
authorized_normalizations: Removed the archive's generic LLM wrapper and reason-generation requests.
Separated the shared end-of-year bonus setting from the four decision procedures.
Restored the omitted list number before potential for productivity in the human-with-algorithmic-option arm.
Locked the four fairness items as primary; retained quantitative and qualitative consideration groups as secondary.

population.simulation_target: Adult evaluating an employee-bonus allocation procedure

materials.participant_role: Act as one adult participant evaluating Company X's bonus-allocation process. Respond for yourself, do not predict the average person, and do not analyze the experiment.
materials.common_scenario: Company X is determining the size of each employee's end-of-year bonus. The company uses the decision process described below and considers a variety of factors.

algorithm_only.label: Algorithm only
algorithm_only.stimulus: Company X relied on an algorithm, a computerized decision-making tool. After a series of computations, the algorithm determined how employee bonuses should be allocated.

algorithm_with_human_adjustment.label: Algorithm with human adjustment
algorithm_with_human_adjustment.stimulus: Company X relied on an algorithm. After its computations determined the allocation, the human resources team could adjust the algorithm's determinations up or down within a margin of 10%.

human_with_algorithmic_option.label: Human with algorithmic option
human_with_algorithmic_option.stimulus: Company X relied on its human resources team. After deliberation, the team determined the allocation and had the option to consider recommendations from an algorithm.

human_only.label: Human only
human_only.stimulus: Company X relied on its human resources team. After a series of deliberations, the team determined how employee bonuses should be allocated.

materials.response_instruction: Rate every item from 1 to 7 using the anchors stated in the question and return only integer item responses in the required JSON structure.

items.text: The way this company determined how to allocate employee bonuses seems fair.
This company's process for deciding which employees receive bonuses was fair.
This decision regarding which employees received bonuses was fair.
The outcome of this decision was fair.
To what degree was profitability to the company part of the decision process? Use 1 for not part of the process and 7 for essential.
To what degree was number of hours worked part of the decision process? Use 1 for not part of the process and 7 for essential.
To what degree was client billing part of the decision process? Use 1 for not part of the process and 7 for essential.
To what degree were leadership skills part of the decision process? Use 1 for not part of the process and 7 for essential.
To what degree was attitude toward clients part of the decision process? Use 1 for not part of the process and 7 for essential.
To what degree was potential for productivity part of the decision process? Use 1 for not part of the process and 7 for essential.

research_restricted.aligned_hypothesis_text: Human-primary bonus procedures are judged fairer than algorithm-primary bonus procedures.
research_restricted.reversed_hypothesis_text: Algorithm-primary bonus procedures are judged fairer than human-primary bonus procedures.
